usageNotes: Permanently destroys a Ceph pool and all data it contains; requires `Sys.Modify` at the root level. By default the pool will not be deleted if it is still in use — pass `force: true` to override this guard. The call returns a task UPID string, so poll the task endpoint to confirm completion before assuming the pool is gone.

examples.summary: Remove an unused replicated pool and its associated Proxmox storage entry

destructiveReason: All objects (VM disks, RBD images, etc.) stored in the pool are permanently erased from the Ceph cluster with no recovery path.
tips: The return value is a UPID task string — follow up with get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status to verify the pool was actually removed.
If `remove_storages` is false (the default), any pveceph-managed Proxmox storage entries pointing at this pool will become broken and must be removed manually from datacenter storage config.
For erasure-coded pools, `remove_ecprofile` defaults to true; set it to false only if the EC profile is shared with another pool.
Ensure no running VMs or containers have disks mapped to this pool before issuing the delete, even with `force: true`.
